deep_dive.1_state_machine: Diff adds transitions: unshipped+uncancelled -> Cancelled=true (with RefundRequested = order.Paid); shipped -> no transition (order returned unchanged, RefundRequested=false); already-cancelled -> no transition (unchanged, RefundRequested=false). Ticket.md only specifies 'let users cancel orders that have not shipped yet' — it does not define behaviour for already-cancelled or paid orders, so those transitions/blocks are additions beyond the literal ticket text (diff.patch:17-30, ticket.md:3).
deep_dive.2_side_effects: Cancel() returns a new Order/CancellationResult; it does not mutate the input order (record `with` expression, diff.patch:27) and does not perform the actual refund or notify any payment system — RefundRequested is only a signal. Where that signal is consumed (payment/refund processing) is outside this diff; responsibility ends at returning the flag. Source: diff.patch:13-31.
deep_dive.3_boundaries: Calling Cancel() twice on an already-cancelled order is explicitly handled (returns original order, RefundRequested=false) per diff.patch:22-25 and tested at Program.cs:60-65. No stale-state issue visible since the function is pure/stateless.
deep_dive.4_errors: Null order throws ArgumentNullException (diff.patch:15, tested Program.cs:76-87). Shipped or already-cancelled orders do NOT throw and DO NOT signal failure via return code — caller must inspect `result.Order.Cancelled` to know whether cancellation actually happened; there is no explicit 'rejected' flag. This matches PR.md:14 ('已出貨時不丟例外') but means callers can silently treat a rejected cancellation as success if they don't check state.
deep_dive.5_types: CancellationResult only exposes `Order` (with bool Cancelled) and `RefundRequested` (bool) — no distinction between 'cancellation succeeded' vs 'cancellation rejected because shipped' vs 'no-op because already cancelled'; caller must diff Cancelled before/after to know the outcome. RefundRequested as bool cannot represent partial refunds or refund amount — ticket.md gives no requirement here so unknown whether this is sufficient.
deep_dive.6_tests: Tests (Program.cs) assert exactly the behaviours the author/AI assumed (PR.md:14), not behaviours traced to ticket.md, which only states the shipped/unshipped rule. The paid/refund and idempotency assertions (Program.cs:33-39, 58-73) are author-assumption-derived, unconfirmed by a rule document.
deep_dive.7_unstated: Unstated requirements accepted by a human: none found — PR.md:15 '已確認／待確認' is blank, so no assumption in PR.md:14 has a recorded human acceptance.
